request.spec: When a newly created owner's telephone shares its area code (first three digits) with five or more existing owners, additionally emit a WARN to the AUDIT logger flagging a possible bulk signup.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

When a newly created owner's telephone shares its area code (first three digits) with five or more existing owners, additionally emit a WARN to the AUDIT logger flagging a possible bulk signup.

agent.result_text:
The full suite passes: **292 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors**, BUILD SUCCESS.

## Summary

Implemented the bulk-signup WARN audit rule in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (the endpoint handling `POST /api/owners`, alongside the existing "Owner created" INFO audit).

**Change** (`src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`):
- After a new owner is persisted, `warnIfPossibleBulkSignup(owner)` computes the owner's **area code** — the first three digits of the telephone after stripping non-digits — and counts existing owners (excluding the new one, by id) sharing that area code.
- If **5 or more** existing owners share it, it emits a `WARN` to the `"AUDIT"` logger: `Possible bulk signup: area code {} shared by {} existing owners; new owner id={}`.
- Returns early (no warning) when the telephone is null or has fewer than three digits.

The threshold and area-code extraction are factored into a named constant and helper for clarity, matching the surrounding audit-logging style. Both new cp20 tests (`coreWarnsOnBulkAreaCode`, `functionalityNoWarnBelowThreshold`) pass, and no existing tests regressed.

I now have the complete picture. Here's the ordered trace.

## Validations & side-effects for `POST /api/owners`

The endpoint is handled by `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (`OwnerRestControllerV1.java:107`), which delegates to `ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner` (`ClinicServiceImpl.java:240`). In execution order:

### A. Before the controller body runs

1. **Authorization** — `@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")`. Caller must have the `OWNER_ADMIN` role, else 403.
2. **Request-body bean validation** — `@Valid @RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto` (`OwnersApi.java:86`). All fields validated before the method executes; failure → 400. Constraints (`OwnerFieldsDto.java`):
   - `firstName`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern(^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}$)`
   - `lastName`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern(^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}\.?$)`
   - `address`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..255)`
   - `city`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..80)`
   - `telephone`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..20)`, `@Pattern(^[0-9 ()-]*$)`
   - `email`: `@Size(max 255)`, `@Email` (optional)

### B. In the controller (`addOwner`)

3. **Map DTO → `Owner`** via `ownerMapper.toOwner` — `id` and `pets` are ignored/unset, so the new owner is "new".
4. **Call `clinicService.saveOwner(owner)`** (transactional) — see section C.
5. **Audit log (side-effect)** — after save, `auditLogger.info("Owner created by user=… id=… membershipNumber=…")`, resolving the current principal name (or `"anonymous"`).
6. **Bulk-signup warning (side-effect)** — `warnIfPossibleBulkSignup(owner)`: derives the telephone area code (first 3 digits); if ≥ 5 *other* existing owners share it, emits `auditLogger.warn("Possible bulk signup: …")`.
7. **`Location` header** set to `/api/owners/{id}`; respond **201 Created** with the owner DTO.

### C. Inside `saveOwner` (the core validations & mutations, in order)

8. **Normalize telephone (side-effect)** — strip all non-digits; the stored value becomes digits-only.
9. **`owner.isNew()` gate** — the following only run for a new owner (always true on this POST path):
   - 10. **Duplicate-telephone check** — `hasIdenticalOwner`: if any existing owner has the same normalized telephone → throw `DuplicateOwnerException`.
   - 11. **Duplicate-email check** — `hasOwnerWithSameEmail`: if email is non-blank and matches an existing owner's normalized email → throw `DuplicateOwnerException("…same email address…")`.
   - 12. **Daily registration limit** — `hasReachedDailyRegistrationLimit`: if ≥ 20 owners already have today's registration date → throw `DailyOwnerRegistrationLimitExceededException`.
   - 13. **City limit** — `hasReachedCityLimit`: if the (normalized) city already holds ≥ 8 owners → throw `CityOwnerLimitExceededException`.
10. **Set `registrationDate` (side-effect)** — if null, default to `LocalDate.now()`.
11. **Resolve/normalize `city` (side-effect)** — reuse an existing owner's exact spelling of a matching city, else title-case the input.
12. **Assign `membershipNumber` (side-effect)** — `(total owner count) + 1`.
13. **Assign `customerCode` (side-effect)** — `<UPPERCASE_CITY>-<NNNN>`, NNNN = (owners in that city) + 1, zero-padded.
14. **Assign `membershipTier` (side-effect)** — `FOUNDING` if fewer than 100 owners exist beforehand, else `STANDARD`.
15. **Assign `namesakeCount` (side-effect)** — count of existing owners sharing the (normalized) last name.
16. **Assign `sharesHousehold` (side-effect)** — true if an existing owner shares the same normalized address + city.
17. **Assign `locality` (side-effect, transient)** — `"local"` if this city is the single most common among existing owners, else `"remote"`.
18. **Persist** — `ownerRepository.save(owner)`. At flush, JPA/Hibernate re-validates the `Owner` entity's own constraints (`Owner.java` / `Person.java`): `@NotEmpty` on firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone, plus telephone `@Digits(integer=10)` and `@Pattern(^[0-9]{10}$)` ("exactly 10 digits") — which now applies to the digits-only normalized value.

Note: the thrown `Duplicate…`/`…LimitExceeded` exceptions are translated to HTTP responses by `ExceptionControllerAdvice`; steps 10–13 short-circuit the whole operation before any side-effect from step 10 onward.
